author: Swinhoe, 1873
habitat: 갈대밭, 작은 물웅덩이, 풀이 우거진 습지
summary: 갈대밭, 작은 물웅덩이, 풀이 무성한 습지에 사는 드문 여름철새로, 서남해안에 서식한다. 물고기, 개구리, 곤충 따위를 주로 잡아먹는다. 물가의 갈대 줄기 위나 풀이 우거진 땅 위에 풀잎과 줄기로 둥지를 짓고 알 5~6개를 낳는다. 세계적으로는 동아시아에 분포한다.

points.en: creamy-white chin and sides of throat
deep reddish-chestnut ear coverts, neck sides and hindneck
single dark brown stripe from chin to breast
dark chestnut from forehead to scapulars (male)
small round white spots on back and scapulars (female)

sexes.female: 이마와 머리꼭대기는 수컷과 같으나, 어두운 밤색 등과 어깨에 작고 둥근 흰 점이 흩어져 있다.

young: 어른 암컷과 비슷하게 몸 윗면이 어두운 밤갈색 바탕에 흰색~담황색 점이 촘촘히 흩어져 있고, 아랫면에는 갈색 세로줄무늬가 굵게 나 있다.

similar.how: 덤불해오라기는 등이 옅은 황갈색이고 날개덮깃이 밝은 담황색이지만, 큰덤불해오라기 수컷은 등과 어깨가 어두운 밤색이고 부리가 더 굵다.

art.subject: Von Schrenck's Bittern (Ixobrychus eurhythmus), adult male in the breeding season, as seen in Korean reedbeds from May to August: crown, hindneck, back and scapulars uniformly dark chestnut-maroon; ear-coverts and neck sides deep reddish-chestnut; chin and sides of the throat creamy white; foreneck, breast and belly buff, with a single dark brown stripe running from the chin down the centre to the breast; breast sides and flanks washed brown; the folded wing is mostly covered by the chestnut scapulars, so the buff wing coverts and blackish flight feathers show mainly in flight; rump paler chestnut-brown. Bill with a dark upper ridge and a paler yellowish lower mandible; yellow iris; legs yellowish-green.
art.pose: standing motionless among reeds at the water's edge, side view
art.scene: Korean summer wetland near the southwest coast: reedbed and small pools with dense grass; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view standing on a reed stem: uniformly dark chestnut from forehead to back and scapulars, deep reddish-chestnut ear-coverts and neck sides, creamy-white chin and throat sides, single dark brown stripe down the buff foreneck to the breast, buff belly, yellowish-green legs

adult female, side view standing: blackish-brown crown, dark chestnut-brown back, scapulars and wing coverts densely scattered with small round white spots, buff underparts with several dark brown streaks down the foreneck and breast, yellowish bill, yellow eye
art.build: Small heron, about 38cm long, slightly larger and darker than Yellow Bittern and much smaller than Black-crowned Night Heron; slim, laterally compressed body for slipping through reeds. Neck fairly long, usually drawn in, but stretched upright with the bill skyward when alarmed. Bill straight and sharp, about as long as the head or a little longer. Legs medium length, yellowish-green, with long toes for clasping reed stems. Very short tail. In flight blackish flight feathers contrast with paler buff wing coverts; legs trail beyond the tail.
avoid: Do not give the male a black cap and a pale yellowish-brown back — that is Yellow Bittern (Ixobrychus sinensis).
Do not paint wholly cinnamon-rufous wings without dark flight feathers — that is Cinnamon Bittern (Ixobrychus cinnamomeus).
Do not put white spots on the adult male; they belong to the female and young birds.
Do not paint a long-necked, long-legged egret shape; it is a small, compact reed bittern.
